item.title: I see Galaxy S26’s AirDrop support as progress, but I just don’t think it changes much
item.description: Samsung supporting AirDrop the Galaxy S26 is the kind of upgrade people will appreciate instantly and buy a phone for almost never.

item.title: Spotify wants you to explore music like never before with SongDNA
item.description: Spotify has launched SongDNA in beta, a feature that maps connections between songs, artists, and samples for deeper music discovery.

item.title: Galaxy Z Fold 8 renders hint at Samsung fixing one big Fold 7 mistake
item.description: Samsung isn't reinventing the wheel with the Galaxy Z Fold 8, but it is making it spin faster — with a 5,000mAh battery, 45W charging, and a 50MP ultrawide finally joining the party.

item.title: My life turned into a subscription trap, but I axed the bad bills with these tricks
item.description: There was a time when subscriptions felt like a novelty. Those were times of (digital) peace. A seamless payment feature on cool new apps that brought unlimited access (for the month). You paid for Netflix, and maybe Spotify, and that was usually about it. Now, it’s streaming, cloud storage, fitness apps, editing apps, AI chatbots, […]

item.title: Slack is getting more features you can count on fingers and toes
item.description: Your entire workflow, now on autopilot (finally).

item.title: If TikTok doomscrolling wasn’t bad enough, it now serves an emoji game in DMs
item.description: TikTok has rolled out a secret emoji game in DMs globally, letting users challenge friends without ever leaving the app.

item.title: Apple extends security updates to older iPhones at risk of hacking
item.description: Apple finally decided older iPhones deserve some love too.

item.title: Google Photos wants to stop you from accidentally ruining your snaps
item.description: Google Photos is redesigning its editor to reduce accidental changes, replacing gesture shortcuts with a more deliberate workflow that prioritizes precision, stability, and fewer unintended edits across Android devices.

item.title: Google Pixel phones might soon block downgrading to an older Android build
item.description: Google may be tightening anti-rollback protection on future Pixel phones, which could stop users from flashing older Android versions even for testing or recovery.

item.title: Scientists built a chip that works in temperatures hotter than lava
item.description: Scientists built a chip that works at 700°C. It could change AI, space travel, and nearly every device you own.

item.title: Volvo’s parent just revealed a $15,000 extended-range EV, and it shows how wide the US value gap has become
item.description: Geely’s new Boyue EREV starts at just $14,900 in China, and it is another reminder that the most aggressive electrified vehicle pricing in the world is happening far away from US buyers.

item.title: Gmail finally lets you change your cringey old usernames
item.description: Google is finally doing the thing Gmail users have been begging for years, which is letting them change the actual username in their Gmail address. This is no longer just an early rollout, as Google says the feature is now available for all Google Account users in the US. So it’s still a limited release, […]

item.title: Land Rover brings Freelander back as EV brand with six models planned
item.description: Land Rover is reviving Freelander as a standalone EV brand with six models planned. The first launch lands this year in China, signaling a fast, tech-heavy push into the premium electric market.

item.title: Catch up on news faster with Google Home’s new Gemini Live
item.description: Google Home’s Gemini Live upgrade adds interactive news you can explore by voice, turning quick updates into deeper conversations that adapt to your questions in real time.
